feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong CV for a senior digital communications leader: clear positioning, credible progression, and relevant technical breadth. It reads polished and substantive, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with limited quantified outcomes beyond scope metrics.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, culminating in director-level leadership and now consulting; this strengthens credibility and shows advancement.  
- Strong alignment between headline, experience, and skills: digital strategy, Drupal/web modernization, analytics, and multimedia all reinforce the target profile.  
- Writing is generally professional and clear, with good use of action verbs and concrete scale indicators like “10,000+ page website” and “3.5 million annual page views.”

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements: include measurable impact on engagement, conversions, email performance, operational efficiency, audience growth, or cost savings—not just responsibilities and platform scope.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; these sections overlap and make the CV feel longer than necessary.  
- Minor style/grammar consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; punctuation in lists is inconsistent (e.g., “web, email, social, and multimedia” vs. no Oxford comma elsewhere); “A2/Learning” is slightly awkward—consider “A2 (learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it reads a bit generic and repeats themes covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it around recent leadership, platform modernization, and mission-driven/public-sector impact would make it sharper.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Lead with current senior value: digital strategy, platform modernization, and cross-channel leadership for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) with a more outcome-oriented framing.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving web, content, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, CMS modernization, and the workflows, governance, and analytics that strengthen complex communications operations. Experienced in advocacy and public-sector messaging, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/systems language overlap with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” is repeated elsewhere; consider “public-sector and advocacy communications” for variety.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and pluralize consistently: “Multi-channel communications,” “Web platform & CMS administration,” “Analytics, reporting & optimization.”
- Replace generic items with more senior, differentiated language: “Digital strategy & platform modernization,” “Editorial systems & governance,” “Cross-functional stakeholder leadership.”
- Consider a tighter rewrite: Digital strategy & platform modernization • Multi-channel communications • Web platform & CMS administration • Editorial systems & governance • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Workflow & systems design • Cross-functional stakeholder leadership • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- If space is tight, drop one lower-priority item such as “Multi-channel communications,” which is already well established elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and Topline Skills, especially digital strategy, multi-channel communications, analytics, and advocacy messaging.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also repeats Soft Skills almost verbatim.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant recent role, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo leadership entry. Tighten it around what is new in the consulting scope, especially hands-on platform delivery and the AI search initiative.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope statement: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and cross-channel governance as an external consultant.”
- Replace generic verbs (“consult,” “build and refine,” “deliver”) with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Designed,” “implemented,” “streamlined,” “launched,” “advised.”
- Consolidate into 3–4 bullets focused on distinct consulting contributions, e.g. Drupal microsites/toolkits, workflow/analytics improvements, AI-enabled search, and technical troubleshooting/front-end implementation.
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of sites/pages supported, publishing time reduced, search relevance gains, toolkit downloads, stakeholder teams served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, and organization-wide communications” repeats the Director role; emphasize external advisory + execution instead.
- Avoid re-stating broad channel oversight across web/email/social unless this consulting role materially changed those functions.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale indicators; it should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in adjacent NACo roles. Focus this item on transformation, infrastructure, and leadership-level results.

Suggested edit
- Replace the opening with a sharper scope statement: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget across a multi-platform ecosystem.”
- Condense channel oversight bullet and prioritize outcomes: combine email/social into one line only if you can add metrics like engagement growth, list growth, CTR, or campaign performance.
- Rewrite for impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Strengthen results language on analytics/governance/video: add measurable outcomes such as reporting time reduced, publishing consistency improved, production costs saved, or event/content volume increased.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this role focused on enterprise leadership and modernization.
- Video expansion may partially duplicate earlier NACo multimedia bullets; frame this as building institutional production capacity, not routine content production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the more recent Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about execution-level leadership and channel growth, with sharper outcomes if you can add metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite opening to distinguish scope: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, leading editorial execution and advocacy messaging before promotion to Director.”
- Tighten bullets around outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching [X]+ county officials and public-sector stakeholders, improving consistency, timeliness and audience reach.”
- Make video bullet more active/measurable: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video series, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Built stronger editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and content delivery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Helped improve…” is too soft and repeats governance/workflow themes already covered in the Director role.
- Weekly video updates are also mentioned in the 2015–2018 role; clarify this was expansion/ownership, not initial creation.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and the most current strengths: enterprise governance, cross-channel leadership, and public-sector strategy.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, outcome-oriented phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Cross-channel content operations leadership
- Public-sector, policy & advocacy communications
- Audience-centered editorial planning
- Stakeholder-aligned messaging strategy
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Cross-channel content operations leadership” to sound more specific and executive.
- Shorten “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” to include “policy” if targeting mission-driven/public affairs roles.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this section to scale from recent roles rather than listing broad capabilities.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” repeat the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is somewhat redundant with editorial workflow/design language elsewhere.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. Make it more strategic and outcome-oriented so it complements recent NACo work rather than repeating tool lists.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing tied to recent impact: “Drupal-led web platform modernization, front-end implementation, API integrations, workflow automation, and AI-enabled search.”
- Trim lower-priority/older items or move them to Technical + IT only; keep the most relevant topline terms: Drupal, CMS modernization, API integrations, workflow automation, AI-enabled search, front-end development.
- Replace “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” with “Front-end development (HTML/CSS/JavaScript)” for concision; drop jQuery unless explicitly required by target roles.
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end development (HTML/CSS/JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, Airtable, and API integrations are already repeated in Technical + IT.
- “CMS modernization” and “workflow automation” also echo Core Competencies; avoid listing them in too many places.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a generic inventory rather than a value-focused skill cluster. Tighten the phrasing and emphasize reporting/decision support over listing every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, and BigQuery for performance measurement, dashboarding, and executive reporting
- Replace “KPI design” with “KPI framework development” or “measurement strategy” to sound more senior and outcome-oriented
- Change “Leadership reporting” to “executive reporting and decision support” for stronger business impact
- Consider final version: “Analytics strategy • KPI framework development • Executive reporting and decision support • GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery • SEO and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies; use this section to be more tool-and-outcome specific, not broader
- Tool names duplicate the Director of Digital Media entry, so avoid overloading this line with the same platforms unless paired with impact language

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong and relevant, but it reads as a generic equipment/task list rather than a senior capability statement. It also overlaps with “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies and several NACo experience bullets.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to outcomes and scope: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera production systems • Virtual event execution”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more senior phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production” to better match Director-level experience.
- Consider adding one impact-oriented qualifier if accurate: “Scalable livestream and hybrid event delivery” or “Recurring advocacy and member-facing video programming.”
- Keep only 4–5 bullets and group related items; “Livestreaming” + “Hybrid and virtual event production” can be streamlined.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This partially duplicates Core Competencies: “Multimedia & live event production.”
- “Studio operations” and “PTZ camera systems” are quite tactical; keep them only if targeting hands-on multimedia roles.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Since recent experience is strongly Drupal-centered, lead with that and make this section more precise or differentiated.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider emphasizing depth: “Drupal (enterprise, migration, modular content) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, add brief qualifiers instead of just names: “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsites/toolkits) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Keep phrasing consistent with other technical lists; avoid title-case variation if not used elsewhere.
- If no meaningful qualifiers can be added, consider trimming GitHub Pages unless it is job-relevant.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills almost exactly; consider merging or using one section for platforms and the other for capabilities.
- Drupal already appears prominently in recent roles, so avoid repeating it elsewhere without added specificity.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and emphasize current, hands-on tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as execution-oriented tools rather than broad coding terms: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group modern tooling separately: “Technical delivery: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, add scope or use case in brief parentheticals: “Cloudflare Workers (edge scripts), GitHub Actions (deployment automation), GTM (tag governance/tracking)”
- Consider dropping version numbers unless required; “HTML” and “CSS” are cleaner than “HTML5/CSS3”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with Topline Skills item “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations • Workflow automation”; differentiate this entry by focusing on implementation tools only
- “Workflow automation” is already covered elsewhere, so avoid repeating it here unless tied specifically to GitHub Actions

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with stronger positioning already established in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” or “Operational Systems & Automation.”
- Tighten to the most relevant tools: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana” and move Slack/Teams to a lighter “Collaboration” category only if space allows.
- If possible, add a brief qualifier instead of a pure list: “Airtable system design • Power Automate and Zapier workflow automation • Jira/Asana project operations.”
- Prioritize tools tied to recent work and systems-building; drop older or lower-signal items like Basecamp/Trello unless they are specifically required by target roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills, so avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Collaboration tools like Slack and Teams add little differentiation given the stronger systems/architecture narrative elsewhere.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful category, but it’s currently just a vendor list with no signal about depth, scale, or relevance. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and platform-focused rather than repeat channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Tighten platform naming for readability: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers instead of more tools: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys (enterprise campaign automation) • Higher Logic (member/community communications) • Mailchimp (newsletter campaigns)
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; if one was limited or older, consider dropping it to sharpen relevance

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters,” “audience engagement,” or campaign management language here; that impact is already covered in Work Experience
- If Dynamics 365 or Higher Logic were not central in recent NACo work, this line may overstate recency compared with stronger web/analytics tools elsewhere

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the bullet is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles that already cover workflows, weekly video, and cross-channel operations. Make this entry more execution-focused and foundational, with sharper scope and any concrete outputs.

Suggested edit
- Reframe around early-career build work: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped launch NACo’s first in-house digital media function…”
- Emphasize distinct contributions not repeated later: website refresh support, livestream/event production, and hands-on multimedia execution.
- Add measurable detail if available: number of livestreams/events produced, cadence of video updates, size of web refresh, or channels supported.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped launch NACo’s first in-house digital media team. Supported a major website refresh and produced day-to-day digital content across web, email, social, and multimedia, including livestreams and recurring video updates. Also helped formalize early production workflows and provided informal supervision/training to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “strengthening workflows” overlaps with 2018–2024 roles; keep workflow language lighter here.
- “weekly video updates” is already covered in the next role; use “recurring video updates” unless this period introduced the format.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the podcast launch, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the “first podcast” achievement and keep the rest concise.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- Trim vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a clearer action, e.g. “produced digital and multimedia content to support program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add scope or result: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or how the podcast expanded communications capacity.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles so progression into digital leadership remains clear.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with the stronger multimedia bullets in 2015–2024 roles.
- Avoid repeating broad web/email/social language here; this role should read as innovation/research + first podcast launch.
